description: Use this when a user asks what rent tenants actually pay or have agreed for a home in a town, area or postcode, how much it costs to rent a flat, house or room there, or how rents compare, in New South Wales, Australia (country AU), Canada (country CA), Catalonia, Spain (country ES), France (country FR), England and Wales (country GB), Ireland (country IE), Norway (country NO), New Zealand (country NZ), Portugal (country PT), Sweden (country SE), Singapore public housing (country SG) or Taiwan (country TW). These are rents actually agreed or paid, taken from official records and statistics: registered tenancies, rental bond lodgements, approved rentals, or official rent statistics built from administrative records of tenancies. Where the source holds individual rents the answer is a median with a typical range (10th–90th percentile) and the number of rents; where the source publishes an average or median (price_type official_statistic) the range fields are null and there is no sample size. Every answer states its unit (rent per month or per week, in the local currency), the period covered, a confidence label, and the official source and licence. How fresh: New South Wales, Australia: monthly; a month's lodgements are published in the first days of the next month; Canada: annual: the October survey is released in the months after it (the October 2025 figures were released on 17 December 2025), and every answer states its survey month; Catalonia, Spain: quarterly; latest published quarter Q1 2026 (dataset updated 30 July 2026); France: annual; the 2025 results were published in October 2026; England and Wales: monthly; each release adds a month about six weeks after it ends (the ONS labels these official statistics in development); Ireland: quarterly; a quarter is published about five months after it ends; Norway: annual; the 2025 survey was published on 22 December 2025; New Zealand: monthly; the files run about two months behind (the October 2026 files end in August 2026) and the latest month can still change; Portugal: quarterly, published about three months after the quarter ends (the 2nd Quarter 2026 figures were released on 29 September 2026); each answer states its quarter; Sweden: annual; the 2026 survey (rents at the start of 2026) was published on 2 October 2026; Singapore public housing: monthly; the previous month's approvals appear in the first days of the next month; Taiwan: the Ministry publishes every 10 days (the 1st, 11th and 21st); a tenancy appears about one to two months after the contract date. Our collector re-reads the releases daily, and answers cover whole calendar months ending at least 30 days before the newest contract in the register. Do not use for asking rents or listings, holiday lets, commercial rent, rent for a specific address, home sale prices, or other countries.

bedrooms.description: Number of bedrooms (0 = studio). Leave out for all sizes. AU: 0 (studio), 1, 2, 3 or 4 (4 means four or more). CA: 0 (bachelor), 1, 2 or 3 (three or more). Leave out for two bedrooms, CMHC's usual headline size; the answer lists every size. ES: not used. FR: 0 (studio) to 3 or more; leave out for all sizes. France counts rooms including the living room, so 1 bedroom = 2 rooms (T2). GB: 1, 2, 3 or 4 (4 means four or more); leave out for all sizes. Studios are not published. Not together with property_type. IE: 1, 2, 3 or 4 (4 means four or more); leave out for all sizes. Studios are not published. NO: not used; use rooms instead (Norway counts rooms). NZ: not applied. MBIE publishes bedroom splits only by unnamed Statistics NZ area codes, not by place name; the answer says so. PT: not supported (INE does not split by bedrooms). SE: required; give the number of ROOMS (Sweden counts rooms, not bedrooms): 1, 2, 3 or 4 (4 means four or more). SG: ignored; HDB counts rooms, not bedrooms. Use flat_type ('4-ROOM'). TW: 0 (studio or open-plan) to 4; 5 means five or more. Leave out for all sizes. Not for rooms.

country.description: AU = Australia, New South Wales only (rental bonds); CA = Canada (CMHC Rental Market Survey, average rents of purpose-built rental units, official statistic); ES = Spain (Catalonia only: INCASOL registered lease deposits); FR = France (observed rents in about 50 agglomerations, local rent observatories); GB = England and Wales (ONS average private rents; Scotland and Northern Ireland are not covered); IE = Ireland (registered tenancies, Residential Tenancies Board); NO = Norway (Statistics Norway rental market survey); NZ = New Zealand (rental bond data from MBIE Tenancy Services; weekly rent in NZD); PT = Portugal (official INE median rent per m² per month of new leases, quarterly, by region and all 308 municipalities); SE = Sweden (Statistics Sweden rent survey); SG = Singapore HDB public-housing flats; TW = Taiwan (Ministry of the Interior actual price registration of rentals: every declared residential tenancy, summarised by city or county and district)

flat_type.description: SG only: HDB flat type, one of 1-ROOM, 2-ROOM, 3-ROOM, 4-ROOM, 5-ROOM, EXECUTIVE ('4 ROOM' also works). Leave out for all types.

house_type.description: Kind of house, for sources that publish houses by type (needed with property_type house there). CA: not used (houses are not published). GB: detached, semi-detached or terraced; required with property_type house. IE: detached, semi-detached or terraced; required with property_type house. NZ: not applied (see property_type). TW: not available (the register does not say detached / semi-detached / terraced); use property_type house.

months.description: How many recent months to include, for sources that hold individual rents. Ignored by sources that publish one figure per quarter or month. AU: 3 or 12 (anything up to 4 uses the latest 3 months, longer uses 12). By default the latest 3 months, widening to 12 when a postcode is quiet. CA: ignored; the figure is for the newest October survey. ES: ignored; the figure is for the latest published quarter. FR: ignored; the figure is for the latest year published. GB: ignored; the figure is for the latest month published. IE: ignored; the figure is for the latest quarter published. NO: ignored; the figure is for the latest year published. NZ: ignored; the figure is for the latest month MBIE has published (about two months behind). PT: ignored; INE publishes one median per quarter, covering the 12 months to the quarter's end (the latest is returned). SE: ignored; the figure is for the latest year published. SG: window of recent months, 1 to 36. Default 12. TW: 12 or 24 whole calendar months; up to 18 gives 12 (24 if a place has too few tenancies in 12), more gives 24. The window ends at the last month that is at least 30 days old.

postcode.description: Postcode, for a precise area. AU: a four-digit NSW postcode, e.g. 2000 (Sydney CBD), 2150 (Parramatta), 2500 (Wollongong). CA: not used; give a town. ES: not used. FR: not used; give the agglomeration as town. GB: not used (rents are published by local authority); give the area name in town. IE: not used (Eircodes are not published); give a town. NO: not used; give a price zone as town. NZ: not used; rents are published by territorial authority and region. PT: not supported (INE publishes by region and municipality); give the municipality as town. SE: not used. SG: not used; give an HDB town. TW: not supported (the register has no postcodes); give the city, county or district as town.

property_type.description: Kind of home: apartment (same as flat), house or room. Default 'any'. AU: apartment (flat or unit), house (includes terraces, townhouses and semi-detached) or any. Rooms are not published. CA: apartment (or flat) means apartment buildings of three or more units; leave out for rows and apartments of three or more units. Houses and rooms are not published. ES: not used (all homes together). FR: apartment (flat), house or leave out for all homes. Single rooms are not published. GB: apartment (flat) or house; leave out for all homes. For house, also give house_type. Rooms are not published. Not together with bedrooms. IE: apartment (flat) or house; leave out for all homes. For house, also give house_type. Rooms are not published. NO: not used (the survey does not split by home type). NZ: not applied. The published place files do not split by dwelling type; the answer covers all new private tenancies and says so. PT: INE publishes one figure for all dwellings; only 'any' has an answer. SE: not used (flats in rented buildings). SG: ignored; every record is an HDB flat. Use flat_type for the size. TW: any (whole homes and self-contained studios), apartment, house (透天厝) or room (a room let separately in a shared home: 分租套房, 分租雅房; kept apart from every other figure).

rooms.description: NO only: number of rooms (living rooms plus bedrooms), 1 to 5 (5 means five or more). Required for Norway.

tenancy.description: FR only: all leases (default), new = leases signed in the last year (what a new tenant faces), existing = leases of one year or more. New leases are published per dwelling type, not per size.

town.description: Town, city or local area. AU: use 'NSW' for the whole state; otherwise give a postcode (NSW rents are published by postcode). CA: required. A town or city of 10,000 people or more, e.g. Toronto, Montréal (or Montreal), Vancouver, Calgary, Edmonton, Ottawa, Winnipeg, Halifax. Add the province to be exact ('London, Ontario'). ES: required; a Catalan municipality, e.g. 'Barcelona', 'Sabadell', 'Girona' (Spanish or Catalan spelling). FR: required. An observed agglomeration: 'Paris' (the city), 'Ile-de-France' (Paris agglomeration), 'Marseille', 'Toulouse', 'Nantes', 'Rennes', 'Strasbourg', 'Bordeaux', 'Montpellier' (about 50 areas; Lyon and Lille are not observed). A name that is not observed returns the full list. GB: required. A local authority (Manchester, Leeds, Camden, Cardiff), an English region (London, North West) or England / Wales. Towns and postcodes are not published; Bristol, Hull etc. match their council area. IE: required. A county ('Dublin', 'Cork'), a town ('Swords, Dublin', 'Galway City') or a Dublin district ('Dublin 6'). NO: required. A price zone: 'Norway' (whole country), 'Oslo', 'Akershus', 'Bergen', 'Trondheim', 'Stavanger', 'large towns', 'medium towns' or 'small towns'. NZ: required. A territorial authority or city ('Wellington', 'Auckland', 'Christchurch', 'Hamilton', 'Dunedin', 'Queenstown-Lakes'), a region ('Canterbury', 'Wellington Region') or 'New Zealand' for the whole country. A name that is both a city and a region (Wellington) gives the city. PT: any municipality ('Lisboa' / 'Lisbon', 'Porto', 'Cascais', 'Faro', 'Funchal', 'Coimbra' ... all 308) or a region ('Algarve', 'Grande Lisboa', 'Madeira', 'Açores'). Omit for Portugal as a whole. Official INE median monthly rent per m² of new leases of the last 12 months (not per home). SE: optional region group: 'Sweden' (default), 'Greater Stockholm', 'Greater Gothenburg', 'Greater Malmo', 'large municipalities' or 'small municipalities'. SG: required, an HDB town such as 'Tampines', 'Bedok' or 'Toa Payoh'. TW: a city or county in English or Chinese ('Taipei' / '台北市' / '臺北市', 'New Taipei', 'Taichung', 'Kaohsiung', 'Tainan', 'Taoyuan', 'Hsinchu City', 'Hsinchu County'), or a district with its city ("Da'an, Taipei", '臺北市大安區', 'Banqiao, New Taipei'). Omit for all of Taiwan. A district name used in several cities ('Zhongzheng', 'Dongqu') needs the city too.

name: pricepaid_rent_prices

outputSchema.description: A price answer: a range or an official statistic with sample size, period, confidence, source and licence.

answer_id.description: Audit trail: a stable id (hash of source id, normalised query, data period and method_version). The same question on the same data gives the same id; keep it with the reasoning that used the figure.

as_of.description: When the answer was produced (ISO 8601); the snapshot date when the official source was down and the answer comes from our copy.

data_age_days.description: Whole days between data_as_of and retrieved_at; null when data_as_of is null.

data_as_of.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the newest data point behind the figure; null when unknown.

evidence.description: Audit trail: what kind of evidence the figure is.

label.description: Short name of the kind of evidence, e.g. 'Recorded sale prices', 'Official published average', 'Posted shelf or pump price', 'Contract award value', 'Regulated reimbursement price'.

meaning.description: One sentence on what this kind of evidence does and does not establish.

extra.description: Source-specific details (for example cheapest stations). extra.stale is true when the answer comes from our copy of the source.

method_version.description: Audit trail: version of the way this source turns raw data into an answer (per source, default '1').

notice.description: Information, not a valuation or offer. Also says when the answer is our copy because the official source did not respond.

period.description: The period the records cover (ISO dates), or the date of the snapshot when the answer comes from our copy.

anyOf.description: The price. Null when there is not enough data to publish a figure (fewer than 5 records) or nothing matched.

measure.description: What value is: median for ranges built from records; average or median for official statistics.

typical_high.description: 90th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

typical_low.description: 10th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

unit.description: What the price is per, e.g. 'per litre', 'per home', 'per kWh'.

value.description: The headline figure. For ranges built from records it equals median.

price_type.description: transaction, posted_pump_price, posted_price, contract_price, reimbursement_price or official_statistic.

query.description: The request as understood, echoed back.

reliability.description: How far to trust the figure as a distribution of real prices. official_with_count = a published official figure with a record count; official_median_no_count = a published average or median with no record count (confidence 'high' there means the publisher is official, not that a count was checked); record_level = 15+ records we hold; thin = 5–14 records; stale = our copy because the official source did not respond; insufficient_data = no figure published.

retrieved_at.description: Audit trail: when ProofPrice produced this answer (ISO 8601). For an answer from our own copy this is now, while as_of is the snapshot date.

sample_size.description: Number of records behind the figure; null when the publisher does not say.

source.description: Where the figure comes from, under which licence, and the attribution line to show.

attribution.description: The attribution line to show with the figure.

url.description: The publisher's page for this data.

statistic.description: Official statistics only: what kind of figure it is and the period the publisher states it for.

status.description: ok = a figure is returned; insufficient_data = fewer than 5 matching records; no_matches = nothing matched.

suggestions.description: Short plain things to try next: widen the period or area, ask for an itemised quote. May be empty.

summary.description: One plain sentence an AI can quote.

title: Rents paid
